questions.prompt: Why is `git push --force-with-lease` safer than `git push --force`?
options: Git checks that the remote branch still matches what you last saw and rejects the push if someone pushed meanwhile
questions.explanation: With `--force-with-lease`, the push is rejected if the remote branch changed since your last fetch, so you cannot overwrite someone else's newer work.

questions.prompt: When do you usually need a force push?
options: After a rebase or another history rewrite on your own branch
questions.explanation: After `git rebase`, after `git reset --hard` when the remote must follow, or when you intentionally rewrite history on your own branch.

source.section: ### When do you usually use force push?

options: switching branches without committing unfinished changes
questions.explanation: Stash saves current work temporarily so you can switch branches without committing; `git stash pop` brings it back.
